claim: High myopia (HM) is a severe form of refractive error that results in irreversible visual impairment and even blindness.
source: High myopia (HM) is a severe form of refractive error that results in irreversible visual impairment and even blindness.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about high myopia based on established clinical knowledge.

claim: Four missense mutations in the ZC3H11A gene (c.412G>A, p.V138I; c.128G>A, p.G43E; c.461C>T, p.P154L; and c.2239T>A, p.S747T) were identified in four patients from a cohort of 1015 patients with HM in adolescents by whole exome sequencing.
source: From a cohort of 1015 patients with HM in adolescents, likely pathogenic missense mutations were identified in the ZC3H11A gene in four patients by whole exome sequencing.
evidence: The claim is supported by whole exome sequencing data from the patient cohort described in the manuscript.

claim: ZC3H11A is a zinc finger and stress-induced protein that plays a significant role in regulating nuclear mRNA export.
source: This gene is a zinc finger and stress-induced protein that plays a significant role in regulating nuclear mRNA export.
evidence: This statement draws from established knowledge about ZC3H11A protein function.

claim: Zc3h11a+/- mice exhibited significant shifts in refraction toward myopia.
source: The Zc3h11a+/- mice exhibited significant shifts in refraction toward myopia.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the mouse model presented in the study.

claim: Myopia-related factors, including Tgfβ1, Mmp2, and Il6, were found to be upregulated in the retina or sclera of Zc3h11a+/- mice.
source: Myopia-related factors, including Tgfβ1, Mmp2, and Il6, were found to be upregulated in the retina or sclera
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and western blot data from the mouse model.

claim: Electroretinography and immunofluorescence staining results showed dysfunction and reduced number of bipolar cells in the retina of Zc3h11a+/- mice.
source: electroretinography and immunofluorescence staining results showed dysfunction and reduced number of bipolar cells in the retina.
evidence: This is supported by ERG measurements and immunofluorescence data presented in the study.

claim: Transmission electron microscopy findings suggest ultrastructural abnormalities of the retina and sclera in Zc3h11a+/- mice.
source: Transmission electron microscopy findings suggest ultrastructural abnormalities of the retina and sclera.
evidence: This is supported by TEM imaging data from the mouse model.

claim: 769 genes were differentially expressed in the retinal transcriptome of Zc3h11a+/- mice compared to wild-type mice.
source: Retinal transcriptome sequencing showed that 769 genes were differentially expressed
evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing data from the retinas of Zc3h11a+/- and WT mice.

claim: Zc3h11a has a negative impact on the PI3K-AKT and NF-κB signaling pathways.
source: Zc3h11a was found to have a negative impact on the PI3K-AKT and NF-κB signaling pathways by quantitative PCR and western blotting.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and western blot data showing pathway changes in Zc3h11a+/- mice.

claim: The prevalence of myopia among the adult population ranges from 10% to 30%, while parts of East and Southeast Asia have reported rates as high as 80–90% among young people.
source: The prevalence of myopia among the adult population ranges from 10% to 30%, while parts of East and Southeast Asia have reported rates as high as 80–90% among young people (Baird et al., 2020; Holden et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: High myopia is characterized by a diopter ≤–6.00 D or an axial length greater than 26 mm.
source: High myopia (HM) is a severe refractive error characterized by a diopter ≤–6.00 D or an axial length greater than 26 mm.
evidence: This is a definitional statement based on established clinical criteria.

claim: By 2050, the number of people with HM worldwide will reach 938 million, accounting for 9.8% of the total population.
source: It is estimated that by 2050, the number of people with HM worldwide will reach 938 million, accounting for 9.8% of the total population.
evidence: This is a projection based on epidemiological modeling, representing speculative future estimates.

claim: HM can trigger a range of adverse ocular changes, such as cataracts, glaucoma, retinal detachment, macular degeneration, and possibly total blindness.
source: HM can trigger a range of adverse ocular changes, such as cataracts, glaucoma, retinal detachment, macular degeneration, and possibly total blindness (Koga et al., 2014; Saw et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Approximately 20 genes with causal associations have been identified in syndromic high myopia (sHM), including ZNF644, SCO2, CCDC111, LRPAP1, SLC39A5, LEPREL1, P4HA2, OPN1LW, ARR3, BSG, NDUFAF7, CPSF1, TNFRSF21, DZIP1, XYLT1, CTSH, GRM6, LOXL3, and GLRA2.
source: To date, approximately 20 genes with causal associations have been identified in sHM, including ZNF644, SCO2, CCDC111, LRPAP1, SLC39A5, LEPREL1, P4HA2, OPN1LW, ARR3, BSG, NDUFAF7, CPSF1, TNFRSF21, DZIP1, XYLT1, CTSH, GRM6, LOXL3, and GLRA2 (Haarman et al., 2022; Tian et al., 2023; Yang et al., 2023; Ye et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Known candidate genes can only explain about 20% of the causes of high myopia.
source: However, known candidate genes can only explain about 20% of the causes of this disease (Cai et al., 2019; Tedja et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: All of the identified ZC3H11A mutations exhibited very low frequencies in the Genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD) and ClinVar.
source: All of the identified mutations exhibited very low frequencies in the Genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD) and ClinVar
evidence: This is supported by database queries and is presented in Table 1.

claim: Most of the identified ZC3H11A mutations display high pathogenicity levels according to SIFT, PolyPhen2, and CADD prediction software.
source: using pathogenicity prediction software SIFT, PolyPhen2, and CADD, most of them display high pathogenicity levels (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by computational predictions presented in Table 1.

claim: The mutations c.412G>A, c.128G>A, and c.461C>T were located in or around a domain named zf-CCCH_3.
source: Among them, c.412G>A, c.128G>A, and c.461C>T were located in or around a domain named zf-CCCH_3 (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis and visualization in Figure 1.

claim: All of the mutation sites were located in highly conserved amino acids across different species.
source: Furthermore, all of the mutation sites were located in highly conserved amino acids across different species (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by multiple sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Four mutations resulted in a higher degree of conformational flexibility and altered the negative charge at the corresponding sites.
source: Four mutations resulted in a higher degree of conformational flexibility and altered the negative charge at the corresponding sites (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by structural modeling data shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: No significant structural differences were observed in retinal fundus images and ocular histomorphology between Zc3h11a+/- mice and wild-type mice at 8 weeks postnatal.
source: Retinal fundus images and ocular histomorphology of Zc3h11a+/- mice at 8 weeks postnatal were assessed against those of their wild-type (WT) counterparts. No significant structural differences were observed (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by fundus photography and histological examination data.

claim: Refraction in Zc3h11a+/- mice was significantly greater than in WT littermates at weeks 4 and 6.
source: Refraction and axial length in Zc3h11a+/- mice were found to be significantly greater than in WT littermates (independent samples t-test, p<0.05; Figure 2A and B). The difference between the two genotypes was statistically significant at weeks 4 and 6.
evidence: This is supported by refractive measurements and statistical analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Axial length in Zc3h11a+/- mice was significantly greater than in WT littermates at weeks 4 and 6.
source: Refraction and axial length in Zc3h11a+/- mice were found to be significantly greater than in WT littermates (independent samples t-test, p<0.05; Figure 2A and B). The difference between the two genotypes was statistically significant at weeks 4 and 6.
evidence: This is supported by axial length measurements and statistical analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The vitreous chamber depth of Zc3h11a+/- mice was deeper than that of WT littermates.
source: Correspondingly, the vitreous chamber depth of Zc3h11a+/- mice was deeper than that of WT littermates (independent samples t-test, p<0.05; Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by OCT measurements and statistical analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: There were no significant differences in the anterior chamber depth, lens diameter, and body weight between Zc3h11a+/- and WT mice.
source: There were no significant differences in the anterior chamber depth, lens diameter, and body weight between the two groups (Figure 2D–F).
evidence: This is supported by measurements shown in Figure 2D-F.

claim: B-wave amplitudes in 7-week-old Zc3h11a+/- mice were significantly lower at dark 3.0 (0.48 log cd·s/m²) and dark 10.0 (0.98 log cd·s/m²) compared to WT mice.
source: Upon dark adaptation, b-wave amplitudes in 7-week-old Zc3h11a+/- mice were significantly lower at dark 3.0 (0.48 log cd·s/m²) and dark 10.0 (0.98 log cd·s/m²) compared to WT mice (Figure 3A and C).
evidence: This is supported by ERG measurements shown in Figure 3A and C.

claim: There were no differences in a-wave amplitudes between the Zc3h11a+/- and WT groups.
source: On the contrary, there were no differences in a-wave amplitudes between the Zc3h11a+/- and WT groups (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by ERG measurements shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The protein abundance of Zc3h11a and PKCα was significantly reduced in the Zc3h11a+/- group.
source: Quantitative analysis of immunofluorescence staining results revealed that the protein abundance of Zc3h11a and PKCα was significantly reduced in the Zc3h11a+/- group (Figure 3G and H).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 3G and H.

claim: The expression level of PKC-α protein in the retina of Zc3h11a+/- mice was significantly reduced, indicating a decrease in the number of bipolar cells.
source: Western blot analysis further showed that the expression level of PKC-α protein in the retina of Zc3h11a+/- mice was significantly reduced, indicating a decrease in the number of bipolar cells (Figure 3I and J).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3I and J, with inference about bipolar cell numbers.

claim: There were no significant differences in the protein abundance of Opsin-1 and Rhodopsin between Zc3h11a+/- and WT mice.
source: However, there were no significant differences in the protein abundance of Opsin-1 and Rhodopsin between the two groups (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both the function and number of retinal bipolar cells were decreased in Zc3h11a+/- mice.
source: Thus, both the function and number of retinal bipolar cells were decreased in Zc3h11a+/- mice.
evidence: This is an inference based on ERG and immunofluorescence data.

claim: In the inner nuclear layer (INL) of the retina, Zc3h11a+/- mouse cells had enlarged perinuclear gaps, perinuclear cytoplasmic edema, and thinned and lightened cytoplasm compared to WT mice.
source: In the inner nuclear layer (INL) of the retina, in contrast to WT mice, Zc3h11a+/- mouse cells had enlarged perinuclear gaps (black arrow), perinuclear cytoplasmic edema (blue arrow), and thinned and lightened cytoplasm (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is supported by TEM imaging data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: In the outer nuclear layer, no significant difference in cell morphology was observed between Zc3h11a+/- and WT mice.
source: However, in the outer nuclear layer, no significant difference in cell morphology was observed between the two groups of mice (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is supported by TEM imaging data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Zc3h11a+/- mice exhibited relatively damaged photoreceptor cell membrane discs, in which the outer layer was detached and sparsely distributed locally.
source: Furthermore, when compared to the WT group, the Zc3h11a+/- mice exhibited relatively damaged photoreceptor cell membrane discs (MB), in which the outer layer was detached and sparsely distributed locally (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: This is supported by TEM imaging data shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: Photoreceptor membrane discs in Zc3h11a+/- mice showed broken membrane discs, as well as some disorganized and loosely arranged ones, with a slight increase in size.
source: There were also a small number of broken membrane discs, as well as some disorganized and loosely arranged ones (red arrow), with a slight increase in size (Figure 4G and H).
evidence: This is supported by TEM imaging data shown in Figure 4G and H.

claim: The structural damage to photoreceptor membrane discs suggests impaired light signal capture, transduction, and compromised visual function in Zc3h11a+/- mice.
source: This suggests impaired light signal capture, transduction, and compromised visual function in Zc3h11a+/- mice.
evidence: This is an inference based on the TEM observations of membrane disc damage.

claim: 303 genes were upregulated and 466 were downregulated in the retinal transcriptome of Zc3h11a+/- mice compared to WT mice.
source: In the retinal transcriptome analysis, 769 genes were differentially expressed (fold change [FC] of at least two and a p-value<0.05) in the Zc3h11a+/- group, of which, 303 were upregulated and 466 were downregulated (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Differentially expressed genes in Zc3h11a+/- mice were significantly enriched in zinc ion transmembrane transport (GO:0071577).
source: Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis revealed significant enrichment of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the following functions: Zinc ion transmembrane transport (GO:0071577) within metal ion homeostasis, associated with retinal photoreceptor maintenance (Ugarte and Osborne, 2001)
evidence: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B and C, with citation to support the functional association.

claim: Differentially expressed genes in Zc3h11a+/- mice were significantly enriched in RNA biosynthesis and metabolism (GO:0006366).
source: RNA biosynthesis and metabolism (GO:0006366) in transcriptional regulation, potentially influencing ocular development
evidence: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data, with speculation about ocular development.

claim: Differentially expressed genes in Zc3h11a+/- mice were significantly enriched in negative regulation of NF-κB signaling (GO:0043124).
source: negative regulation of NF-κB signaling (GO:0043124) in inflammatory modulation, a pathway involved in scleral remodeling (Xiao et al., 2025)
evidence: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data, with citation to support the functional association.

claim: Differentially expressed genes in Zc3h11a+/- mice were significantly enriched in calcium ion binding (GO:0005509).
source: calcium ion binding (GO:0005509), critical for phototransduction (Krizaj and Copenhagen, 2002)
evidence: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data, with citation to support the functional association.

claim: Differentially expressed genes in Zc3h11a+/- mice were significantly enriched in zinc ion transmembrane transporter activity (GO:0005385).
source: zinc ion transmembrane transporter activity (GO:0005385), participating in retinal zinc homeostasis (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: The differentially expressed genes in the Zc3h11a+/- group were primarily involved in the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway, MAPK signaling pathway, and neuropsychiatric disease according to KEGG pathway enrichment analysis.
source: KEGG pathway enrichment analysis indicated that the DEGs in the Zc3h11a+/- group were primarily involved in the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway, MAPK signaling pathway, and neuropsychiatric disease (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by KEGG pathway enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: PI3K-AKT is one of the most important pathways for cell survival, division, autophagy, and differentiation.
source: PI3K-AKT is one of the most important pathways for cell survival, division, autophagy, and differentiation (Alzahrani, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: ZC3H11A can regulate the NF-κB pathway at the level of IκBα mRNA export in ZC3-KO cells.
source: Meanwhile, it has been found that ZC3H11A can regulate the NF-κB pathway at the level of IκBα mRNA export in ZC3-KO cells (Darweesh et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: IκBα is a critical protein that governs NF-κB function predominantly within the cytoplasmic compartment and plays a pivotal role in inhibiting the activation of NF-κB.
source: IκBα is a critical protein that governs NF-κB function predominantly within the cytoplasmic compartment. It plays a pivotal role in inhibiting the activation of NF-κB (Dyson and Komives, 2012; Manavalan et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: AKT promotes IκBα phosphorylation to undergo degradation, which enhances the nuclear translocation of NF-κB.
source: In addition, AKT promotes IκBα phosphorylation to undergo degradation, which enhances the nuclear translocation of NF-κB (Alzahrani, 2019; Torrealba et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The expression levels of PI3K, p-AKT/AKT, and NF-κB were significantly upregulated in the retina of Zc3h11a+/- mice.
source: The expression levels of PI3K, p-AKT/AKT, and NF-κB were significantly upregulated, while Zc3h11a and IκBα were downregulated in Zc3h11a+/- mice (Figure 6A–L).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Zc3h11a and IκBα expression were downregulated in the retina of Zc3h11a+/- mice.
source: The expression levels of PI3K, p-AKT/AKT, and NF-κB were significantly upregulated, while Zc3h11a and IκBα were downregulated in Zc3h11a+/- mice (Figure 6A–L).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The mRNA expression levels of IκBα in the nucleus of all four mutant types (ZC3H11AV138I, ZC3H11AG43E, ZC3H11AP154L, and ZC3H11AS747T) were significantly reduced compared to the WT.
source: Meanwhile, through transfection of overexpression mutant plasmids, it was found that compared to the WT, the mRNA expression levels of IκBα in the nucleus of all four mutant types (ZC3H11AV138I, ZC3H11AG43E, ZC3H11AP154L, and ZC3H11AS747T) were significantly reduced (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data from transfection experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: ZC3H11A likely contributes to myopia pathogenesis by inhibiting both PI3K-AKT and NF-κB signaling pathways.
source: These results strongly suggest that ZC3H11A likely contributes to myopia pathogenesis by inhibiting both PI3K-AKT and NF-κB signaling pathways.
evidence: This is an inference based on the pathway analysis and expression data.

claim: In animal models of myopia, intraocular concentrations of Tgfβ1 are elevated, especially in the retina and sclera.
source: In animal models of myopia, it has been established that intraocular concentrations of Tgfβ1 are elevated (Chen et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2022), especially in the retina and sclera.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The abnormal expression of matrix metalloproteinase-2 (Mmp2) and interleukin-6 (Il6) can induce myopia, and these are regulated by NF-κB.
source: The abnormal expression of matrix metalloproteinase-2 (Mmp2) and interleukin-6 (Il6) can induce myopia, and these are regulated by NF-κB (Libermann and Baltimore, 1990; Wu and Schmid-Schönbein, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: qPCR analysis showed increased expression of Tgfb1, Mmp2, and Il6 in the sclera and retina of Zc3h11a+/- mice compared with WT mice.
source: qPCR analysis showed increased expression of Tgfb1, Mmp2, and Il6 in the sclera and retina of Zc3h11a+/- mice compared with WT mice (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Western blot results showed increased expression levels of Tgfβ1 and Mmp2 in the retinas of Zc3h11a+/- mice.
source: The western blot results showed increased expression levels of Tgfβ1 and Mmp2 in the retinas of Zc3h11a+/- mice (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Scleral collagen fibers in Zc3h11a+/- mice were disorganized over a large area with irregular transverse and longitudinal arrangement.
source: Scleral TEM results suggested that scleral collagen fibers in Zc3h11a+/- mice were disorganized over a large area with irregular transverse and longitudinal arrangement (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by TEM imaging data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Zc3h11a mutation may participate in the development of myopia by inhibiting the NF-κB signaling pathway, thereby upregulating the expression of myopia-related factors such as Mmp2 and Il6.
source: These results further corroborate that Zc3h11a+/- mice exhibit a myopic phenotype, and that Zc3h11a mutation may participate in the development of myopia by inhibiting the NF-κB signaling pathway, thereby upregulating the expression of myopia-related factors such as Mmp2 and Il6.
evidence: This is an inference based on the pathway and expression data.

claim: ZC3H11A is a new candidate gene associated with HM in a cohort of Chinese Han individuals.
source: Overall, this study has provided four key findings. First, it was confirmed that the ZC3H11A is a new candidate gene associated with HM in a cohort of Chinese Han individuals.
evidence: This is supported by the WES data from the patient cohort.

claim: Changes in Zc3h11a expression affect retinal function, particularly in bipolar cells.
source: Second, changes in Zc3h11a expression were found to affect retinal function, particularly in bipolar cells.
evidence: This is supported by ERG and immunofluorescence data.

claim: Changes in Zc3h11a expression cause alterations in numerous signaling pathways, the most notable being the PI3K-AKT and NF-κB pathways.
source: Third, changes in Zc3h11a expression were found to cause alterations in numerous signaling pathways, the most notable being the PI3K-AKT and NF-κB pathways.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq, qPCR, and western blot data.

claim: Changes in Zc3h11a expression cause changes in the myopia-related genes Tgfβ1, Mmp2, and Il6.
source: Fourth, changes in Zc3h11a expression were found to cause changes in the myopia-related genes Tgfβ1, Mmp2, and Il6.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and western blot data.

claim: Abnormal expression of Zc3h11a triggers nuclear translocation defects of IκBα, thereby exerting negative feedback regulation of the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway and inhibiting the NF-κB signaling pathway.
source: The above results suggest that abnormal expression of Zc3h11a triggers nuclear translocation defects of IκBα, thereby exerting negative feedback regulation of the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway and inhibiting the NF-κB signaling pathway.
evidence: This is an inference based on the pathway analysis and expression data.

claim: The increase in Tgfβ1 in myopic eyes stimulates the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway, which leads to activation of the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway, resulting in downstream degradation of IκBα after phosphorylation.
source: At the same time, the increase in Tgfβ1 in myopic eyes stimulates the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway, which leads to activation of the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway, resulting in downstream degradation of IκBα after phosphorylation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the pathway analysis and expression data.

claim: Degradation of IκBα increases the nuclear translocation of NF-κB.
source: This, in turn, increases the nuclear translocation of NF-κB.
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge of NF-κB regulation.

claim: Zc3h11a promotes the myopia-associated factor Tgfβ1 by acting directly or indirectly on both the PI3K-AKT and NF-κB signaling pathway-mediated stress reactions and the expression of Mmp2 and Il6, which together, caused the development of early HM.
source: To sum up, Zc3h11a promotes the myopia-associated factor Tgfβ1 by acting directly or indirectly on both the PI3K-AKT and NF-κB signaling pathway-mediated stress reactions and the expression of Mmp2 and Il6, which together, caused the development of early HM (Figure 8).
evidence: This is an inference based on the comprehensive analysis of all experimental data, with a model shown in Figure 8.

claim: ZC3H11A is a member of the zinc finger protein gene family.
source: This particular gene is a member of the zinc finger protein gene family.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of gene families.

claim: Multiple zinc finger protein genes (e.g. ZNF644, ZC3H11B, ZFP161, ZENK) are associated with myopia or HM.
source: Multiple zinc finger protein genes (e.g. ZNF644, ZC3H11B, ZFP161, ZENK) are associated with myopia or HM.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from the literature.

claim: ZC3H11B (a human homolog of ZC3H11A) and five GWAS loci correlate with AL elongation or HM severity.
source: Of these, ZC3H11B (a human homolog of ZC3H11A) and five GWAS loci (Schippert et al., 2007; Shi et al., 2011; Szczerkowska et al., 2019; Tang et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2004) correlate with AL elongation or HM severity.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Proteomic studies suggest ZC3H11A involvement in the TREX complex, implicating RNA export mechanisms in myopia pathogenesis.
source: Proteomic studies further suggest ZC3H11A involvement in the TREX complex, implicating RNA export mechanisms in myopia pathogenesis.
evidence: This is based on proteomic studies, representing established knowledge.

claim: ZC3H11A is involved in stress-induced responses.
source: Additionally, it has been suggested that this protein is involved in stress-induced responses (Younis et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Dysfunction of ZC3H11A results in enhanced NF-κB signaling through defective IκBα protein expression, which is accompanied by upregulation of numerous innate immune- and inflammation-related mRNAs, including IL8, IL6, and TNF in vitro.
source: Dysfunction of ZC3H11A results in enhanced NF-κB signaling through defective IκBα protein expression, which is accompanied by upregulation of numerous innate immune- and inflammation-related mRNAs, including IL8, IL6, and TNF in vitro (Jimi et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Patients with myopia have a higher proportion of inflammation-associated cells, including neutrophils.
source: Moreover, patients with myopia have a higher proportion of inflammation-associated cells, including neutrophils, while those with moderate myopia show strained immune system function (Lin et al., 2016; Qi et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Patients with moderate myopia show strained immune system function.
source: Moreover, patients with myopia have a higher proportion of inflammation-associated cells, including neutrophils, while those with moderate myopia show strained immune system function (Lin et al., 2016; Qi et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Some traditional Chinese medicines can control myopia progression by suppressing AKT and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory reactions.
source: Conversely, some traditional Chinese medicines can control myopia progression by suppressing AKT and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory reactions (Chen et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: ZC3H11A is involved in the export and posttranscriptional regulation of selected mRNA transcripts required to maintain metabolic processes in embryonic cells.
source: ZC3H11A is involved in the export and posttranscriptional regulation of selected mRNA transcripts required to maintain metabolic processes in embryonic cells; these are essential for the viability of early mouse embryos (Younis et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: In studies of chickens, mice, and humans, the zinc finger protein ZENK was found to play a role in the development of refractive myopic excursion and lengthening of the ocular axis.
source: In studies of chickens, mice, and humans, the zinc finger protein ZENK was found to play a role in the development of refractive myopic excursion and lengthening of the ocular axis.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from the literature.

claim: Early growth response gene type 1 Egr-1 (the human homolog of ZENK) activates the TGF-β1 gene by binding to its promoter, which is thought to be associated with myopia.
source: Moreover, early growth response gene type 1 Egr-1 (the human homolog of ZENK) activates the TGF-β1 gene by binding to its promoter, which is thought to be associated with myopia (Baron et al., 2006; Xiao et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: ZNF644 has been identified by WES as causing HM in Han Chinese families.
source: Another zinc protein finger protein 644 isoform, ZNF644, has recently been identified by WES as causing HM in Han Chinese families (Shi et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Reduced protein expression of Zc3h11a was reported in a unilateral induced myopic mouse model.
source: which is consistent with previous studies reporting reduced protein expression of Zc3h11a in a unilateral induced myopic mouse model (Fan et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: In vertebrate models, refractive development and ocular axial growth are visually controlled.
source: In vertebrate models, refractive development and ocular axial growth are visually controlled (Wallman and Winawer, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The regulation of axial length or refractive error occurs through complex light-dependent retina-to-sclera signaling.
source: The regulation of axial length or refractive error occurs through complex light-dependent retina-to-sclera signaling (Tkatchenko and Tkatchenko, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Optical scatter information is processed by the retina and then converted into molecular signals that regulate peripheral retinal growth and scleral connective tissue renewal, ultimately affecting the growth rate of the posterior segment of the eye.
source: Optical scatter information is processed by the retina and then converted into molecular signals that regulate peripheral retinal growth and scleral connective tissue renewal, ultimately affecting the growth rate of the posterior segment of the eye (Harper and Summers, 2015; Tkatchenko et al., 2006; Tkatchenko et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: All cell types of the retina contain myopia-related genes and retinal circuitry driving refractive error.
source: All cell types of the retina contain myopia-related genes and retinal circuitry driving refractive error.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from the literature.

claim: Damage to retinal bipolar cells may impair visual signal processing and transduction through neural circuit alterations, thereby contributing to the pathogenesis of HM.
source: Thus, damage to retinal bipolar cells may impair visual signal processing and transduction through neural circuit alterations, thereby contributing to the pathogenesis of HM.
